subject: Objectives charter: executive briefing and endorsement
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Beth Turner <beth@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Objectives charter: executive briefing and endorsement

Team — attaching the first-pass objectives charter for the quarter. This is the version I want leadership to endorse so we can lock the QBR slate and start routing the cross-functional work. Summary below and a link to the editable doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A_obj-charter-draft

High-level ask: please review and indicate endorsement or top-3 concerns by EOD Friday (May 7). If you don't respond I will assume tacit approval and move to finalize for the Deck.

Proposed company objectives (top-line):
1) Deliver predictable inference latency at 99th pct <= 120ms for hosted small-gen models (customer-facing SLO).
   - KR1.1: Reduce median token latency by 15% vs baseline.
   - KR1.2: Reach 99p latency <= 120ms on standard 2k token profile on dedicated tier.
2) Reduce per-token inference cost for enterprise workloads by 20% through batching and quantization profiles.
   - KR2.1: Ship autoscaling + batching config for top 3 enterprise customers.
   - KR2.2: Validate quantized model profiles on 3 hardware families with <3% quality delta.
3) Improve reliability & auditability for Private deployments (security/compliance runway).
   - KR3.1: Complete extended audit logs and KMS integration in private control plane.
   - KR3.2: Pilot SOC2 evidence pack with two regulated customers (Acme Analytics is first pilot).

Notes:
- I attached ObjCharter_v1.pdf with the full context and ramp timelines.
- QBR dry-run windows are in the calendar invite (QBR_dryrun_schedule.ics) — please mark availability.

Open decisions we need leadership to resolve:
- KR2 target: is 20% reduction aggressive given expected model revisions?
- Dedicated capacity commit for top enterprise tier (cost tradeoffs) — need a go/no-go by May 14.
- Signoff for Acme Analytics pilot (Beth is cc'd for context).

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ObjCharter_v1.pdf, QBR_dryrun_schedule.ics

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Beth Turner <beth@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Objectives charter: executive briefing and endorsement

Camila — quick first pass notes inline and top-level: I like the framing, but want to flag two concerns.

Inline: 
> KR2.2: Validate quantized model profiles on 3 hardware families with <3% quality delta.
I suggest loosening to <4% for initial pilots (we risk pushing customers away if we aggressively quantify without more evals). Can we scope a 2-phase validation (pilot then scale)?

Top-level asks: 
- Please add an explicit headcount ask for one FW/release engineer to the objective so we can track resourcing (without that we won't meet KR1/KR2 timelines).
- For the Acme Analytics SOC2 pilot: confirm the expected data retention window and whether they require an on-prem connector (Beth, can you confirm?).

If we adopt the 2-phase plan for KR2 I'll endorse the charter. Happy to jump on a 20-minute call if useful.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Strategy & Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks Camila — read the doc this morning. Short response:
- I'm supportive of the latency objective and the reliability runway.
- Agree with Hannah on relaxing KR2.2 to <4% for the pilot phase; the risk/cost tradeoff otherwise becomes heavy.
- I can sign off on the charter if we add the explicit headcount line and a short appendix that outlines the plan to validate quantized profiles (test harness, datasets, evaluation rubric).

I'll sync with infra next week to confirm resource availability; we may need a small re-prioritization but it's doable.
